title: Eisenstein criterion at a prime ideal
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative integral domain, $\mathfrak p\subsetneq A$ a prime ideal, and $f\in A[X]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] a polynomial of positive degree. Assume that its leading coefficient is not in $\mathfrak p$, that every coefficient of smaller degree lies in $\mathfrak p$, and that its constant coefficient is not in $\mathfrak p^2$. Assume also that $f$ is primitive: whenever a constant polynomial $c\in A$ divides $f$, $c$ is a unit of $A$. Then $f$ is irreducible in $A[X]$, meaning that it is a nonzero nonunit and in any factorization one factor is a unit.
